newsitem.title: DUBAI: First Iraqi oil tanker set to leave Mina al-Bakr.
newsitem.headline: First Iraqi oil tanker set to leave Mina al-Bakr.

text.p: The first tanker to export crude from Iraq's Mina al-Bakr terminal in the northern Middle East Gulf will leave the terminal late on Tuesday, a Gulf shipping source said on Tuesday.
The VLCC Star of Africa, carrying crude on behalf of U.S. Coastal Corp, completed loading Tuesday morning, the same source said.
"It completed loading this morning...It will leave later tonight at low tide," the source said.

The second tanker at the terminal, the 272,000 deadweight tonnes Leonidas which industry sources say has been chartered by U.S. independent oil firm Bayoil, is expected to complete its loading on Tuesday, the shipping source added.
Leonidas was expected to sail on Wednesday.
Iraq exported its first oil cargo in six years on December 16 from the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan under an "oil-for-food" deal agreed with the United Nations.
Industry sources said that the loading rate at Mina al-Bakr had been successfully increased after an initial slow start.
Star of Africa docked at the terminal on December 14.
The U.N. has so far approved six crude contracts under the deal where Iraq is permitted to sell $2 billion of its oil over six months on a renewal basis for humanitarian supplies.
These are Coastal, Bayoil, Turkish state refiner TUPRAS, Dutch trading firm Trafigura, Italian refiner Oil Energy and France's Elf Aquitaine. Gulf industry sources said on Tuesday.
